full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rashid J: Defendant No. 1 obtained the Rule upon making a revision application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure against judgment and decree dated 18-2-1990 passed by District Judge at Pirojpur in Title Appeal No. 8 of 1989 affirming those dated 31-12-1988 passed by Assistant Judge at Sadar in Pirojpur in Title Suit No. 50 of 1988, which decreed the suit in its entirety.

2. Opposite party Nos. 1 to 10 as plaintiffs on or about 12-3-1988 instituted the suit against the petitioner and others for a decree of declarations, inter alia, that

(a) order dated 14-1-1988 passed in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 described in schedule 'Kha' was illegal, void, inoperative and not binding upon the plaintiffs;

(b) the plaintiffs have got title in the suit land; and

(c) defendant No. 2 Ramendra Nath @ Rabindranath Biswas was 'Benamder' of lshaque Ali Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs in respect of the sale deeds dated 28-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 described in schedule 'Ga' to the plaint.

3. The suit land described in five items of schedule 'Ka' to the plaint comprises of about 4.44 acres of land.

4. Plaint case, in short, is that land of RS Khatian Nos. 197, 261 and 783 as described in schedule 'Ka' originally belonged to Nani Bala, who transferred said land to Bimal Krishna Debnath. Bimal Debnath then transferred the land to Ishaque Ali Miah, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs by a registered 'Kabala' dated 12-4-1973.

5. Defendant No. 4 on 13-12-1973 got a decree in Title Suit No. 56 of 1972 of Second Court of Subordinate Judge at Barishal in respect of 1.11 acres of the suit land on the basis of 'Pattan' claimed to have been obtained by his mother. When the predecessor of the plaintiffs challenged the decree by instituting a suit, defendant No.4, on compromise, transferred 53.75 decimals of the suit land by a 'Kabala' dated 15-8-1987 to plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7.

6. Land of RS Khatian No. 128 belonged to Rebuti Ranjan Ghosh, who transferred said land to Ishaque Ali by a registered 'Kabala' dated 18-12-1972. Ishaque Ali purchased the land in the 'Benami' of defendant No. 2 Ramendra Nath. Similarly, while Indobhushan and Sarala Bibia were owners in possession of land of RS Khatian No. 147 they transferred said land to Ishaque Ali by a registered deed dated 1-4-1974 in the name of 'Benami' of said defendant No.2.

7. Thus, Ishaque Ali, said predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs, acquired good title and possession in the entire land of schedule 'ka'. Then, he died leaving the plaintiffs as his only heirs and legal representatives. The plaintiffs possessed those lands through 'Bargaders'.

8. In 1394 BS, the suit land was given to defendant No. 1 for 'Borga' cultivation. When defendant No. 1 refused to give 'Borga' share to the plaintiffs, they started CR Case being No. 17 of 1988 in the local Upazila Magistrate Court. During the prosecution of the case defendant No. 1 declared that he had title and possession in the suit land, which was recorded in the record of rights in the name of his father Hashem Ali. The plaintiffs also came to know that Hashem Ali obtained an ex parte decree in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 and got the record corrected in his name on the basis of the decree.

9. Further case of the plaintiffs is that defendant No. 2 in collusion with defendant No. 1 refused to execute a deed relinquishing all claims in the suit land in their favour. They claimed to be in possession of the entire suit land for more than twelve years and defendants had no title or possession in the suit land.

10. Defendant No. 1 alone contested the suit by filing a written statement. His case in short, is that his father Hashem Ali Sheikh got the suit land by way of 'Pattan'. When he was thus owner in possession of the suit land, the suit land was wrongly recorded in the names of original owners in the survey under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. Hashem Ali was then constrained to institute Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 against original tenants including those the plaintiffs claimed to have acquired title for declaration of title practically for correction of the record of rights and got a decree on 28-10-1957. On the basis of the decree, Hashem Ali made an application being Miscellaneous Case No. 4222/60-61 under section 54 for correction of the record and got an order on 28-3-1961. Then, the record was finally corrected in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 and the suit land was recorded in his name. Hashem Ali possessed 5.02 acres including the suit land until his death and after him defendant No. 1 continued possessing said land as his sole heir for more than 12 years by making a dwelling and living therein; and also by cultivation.

11. The plaintiffs started a false criminal case under sections 406 and 420 and destroyed by setting fire the huts of defendant No. 1 on the suit land and looted away his belongings by hired goons. The defendant filed a criminal case being GR Case No. 33 of 1988 in the Court of the Upazila Magistrate against the plaintiffs over trespass and looting, which was pending. Having found that they had no hope in their criminal case, the plaintiffs instituted instant suit on false allegations. They got no title or possession in the suit land.

12. On the party pleadings following issues were settled:

(a) Whether the suit as framed was maintainable?

(b) Whether the suit was barred by limitation?

(c) Whether the suit was bad for defect of parties?

(d) Whether the suit was hit by the proviso to section 42 of the Specific Relief Act?

(e) Had the plaintiffs any right, title, interest or possession in the suit land?

(f) Whether the order dated 14-1-1988 passed in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 was binding upon the plaintiffs? and (g) What relief or reliefs the plaintiffs were entitled to?

13. Plaintiffs examined six witnesses while defendant No. 1 examined five witnesses in support of their respective cases. Plaintiffs adduced number of documents, which were marked as exhibit 1 to 1(d), 2-2(ka) 3, 4 to 4(d) and 5 to 7 and while those of defendant marked as exhibit A to A(3), B to B(1) and C.

14. Trial Court on the evidence on record decreed the suit as prayed for. On appeal therefrom at the instance of defendant No.1, the appeal was dismissed and decree of the trial Court affirmed by the impugned judgment and decree. Hence this Rule. Mr Syed Mofizur Rahman, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the suit as framed in the manner and form was not maintainable and also barred by limitation.

15. In the absence of any declaration sought for against the decree dated 28-10-1957 passed in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 and order dated 28-3-1961 passed in Case No. 4222/60-61 for correction of the record of rights, he submits, the plaintiffs are not entitled to any decree.

16. He submits that in view of the fact that the record of rights under the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act was wrongly prepared in the names of previous tenants, which was ultimately corrected and mutated in the name of Hashem Ali, father of defendant No.1 by order dated 14-1-1988 passed in case No. 9P/87-88 on the basis of actual physical possession, both the Courts below erred in law in decreeing the suit without taking into consideration of long possession of defendant No. 1 in the suit land, which occasioned failure of justice.

17. He submits that finding by the Courts below that defendant No.2 was a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali and defendant No. 1 was a 'Borgadar' of the plaintiffs are based on no evidence, oral and documentary, and the decree passed thereupon is liable to be set aside. In support, he cited 6 MLR 199, Abul Quashem and another vs Hafizur Rahman and others.

18. Mr Sadananda Rana, learned Advocate for plaintiffs-opposite parties, on the other hand, submits that both the courts below decreed the suit as prayed for and such decree is now binding in revision.

19. He submits that the petitioner failed to make out any case against the concurrent findings of the Courts below that defendant No. 2 was a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali and defendant No. 1 possessed the suit land as a 'Borgadar' under the plaintiffs to justify any interference by this Division.

20. He submits that defendant No. 2 already' admitted to be a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali Mia by presenting an application in the Court. Upon such admission, there was no difficulty for the Courts below to hold that defendant No.2 was a 'benamder' of said Ishaque Ali.

21. Lastly, he submits that even if defendant No.2 is found to be in possession but his possession being constructive possession of a 'Borgadar', such possession cannot resist the suit of the plaintiffs from being decreed.

22. The issue facing me is whether or not the appellate judgment and decree affirming those of the trial Court decreeing the suit in its entirety are well founded on the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence, oral and documentary, on record and in law.

23. I have perused the entire record.

24. As stated at the outset, the plaintiffs instituted the suit for declarations that they have got title in the suit land, that defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath was 'Benamdar' of their father Ishaque Aii in respect of sale deeds dated 28-12-1972 and 1-4- 1974 and that the order dated 14-1-1988 passed in Mutation Case No. 9P/87-88 was illegal, void and not binding upon them.

25. Needless to say that in order to succeed in the suit the plaintiffs would have first to establish their title and then, possession in the suit land. It is the case of the plaintiffs that their predecessor-in- interest, Ishaque Ali acquired title by way of purchase in the name of defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath by two registered sale deeds dated 18-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 and defendant No. 4 Abdul Salek transferred 53.75 decimals by a registered sale deed dated 15-8-1987 to the plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7 on the basis of a compromise in the suit brought by him.

26. In support, the plaintiffs adduced five 'kabalas' dated 12-4-1973, 28-12-1972, 15-8-1987, 29-12-1972 and 1-4-1974, which were marked as Exhibits 1 to 1(d). All the deeds were produced in original.

27. Kabala dated 12-4-1973, Exhibit 1 shows transfer by Bimal Krishna Debnath to Ishaque Ali of 2.44 acres of plot Nos. 431, 432 and 659 of SA Khatian No. 324, 23 decimals of plot No. 520 of SA Khatian No. 277 and 22 decimals of plot No. 520 in total 2.89 acres. By sale deed dated 28-12-1972, exhibit 1(a) said land appears to be transferred to Bimal Krishna Debnath by Nani Bala Ghoshe. Sale deed dated 1578-1987, Exhibit 1 (b) shows transfer of 53.75 decimals of plot No. 659 of SA Khatian No. 324 by Abdus Salek (defendant No.4) to plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7. Sale deed 28-12-1972, exhibit 1(c) evidences transfer of 67 decimals of plot Nos. 431 and 432 of SA Khatian 509 by Rebuti Romen Ghosh and sale deed dated 1-4-1974, exhibit 1(d) transferring 73 decimals of plot No. 431, 432, 433 and 658 of SA Khatian 147 by Indobhushan to Ramendra Nath Biswash, son of Birendra Nath. Said deeds cover 4.8275 acres of land.

28. But the plaintiffs claimed 4.44 acres only. Of the suit land, in Item 5 of schedule "Ka' the plaintiffs claimed 1.46 acre of SA Khatian No. 147. In support or 1.46 acre, I find only evidence adduced is a deed dated 1-4-1974, Exhibit-1 (d), which is claimed to have been purchased by their father Ishaque Ali in the 'Benami' of defendant No. 2 Ramendra Nath and covers 73 decimals of land only, For the rest of 7 decimals no other evidence was adduced. Similarly, the plaintiffs claimed that 67 decimals of SA Khatian No. 509, was purchased by Ishaque Ali in, the 'Benami' of said defendant No. 2.

29. In support of the 'Benami' transaction, the plaintiffs examined plaintiff No. 1 Raji Haider as PW 1 Who claimed to be 25 years old on 13-12-1988, the date of his deposition. He said that their father purchased said land (67+73=140) in the name of defendant No. 2, their 'Karmachari'. Their father paid the price and got possession of said land.

PW 6 Yusuf Ali tried to corroborate PW 1 on 'Benami 'in his chief saying that in the deed dated 29-12-1972, Exhibit-1(c) he was a witness and he saw Ishaque Ali paid money to Rebuti Ranjan in his presence. But, in cross, he said that he was a moharar of Advocate Aftab Miah, Ismail Miah and Bimal Krishna Sen. At the time of deposition he gave up the work. He went to Barishal for his own works, nobody took him to Barishal. At the request of Ishaque Ali, he became a witness to the deed. But more than once, he said that he could not say how much money father of the plaintiffs paid to Rebuti Ranjan. Close scrutiny of the deposition of PW 6 does not inspire any confidence in his evidence on the passing of consideration for the deed dated 28-12-1972, Exhibit-1(c). Courts below missed to scrutinise the evidence of such chance witness and failed to consider the fact that such witness could not be a witness to the 'Benami' transaction.

30. Plaintiffs could not adduce any other' evidence to prove their case on 'Benami'. They could not even find anyone to prove payment of consideration by Ishaque Ali for the deed dated 1-4-1974, Exhibit 1(d).

31. Defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath did not turn up to support the case of the plaintiffs that Ishaque Ali purchased 1.40 acre of land in his name. Plaintiffs however, tried to rely upon an application filed on behalf of Ramendra Nath in the suit. But nobody came forward to prove such application was indeed, filed by defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath. In the absence of any proof, such application could not be treated to be any step taken in the suit by any party in the suit and far less than to be treated as an evidence and was, in fact, not admitted into evidence.

32. But upon such application that Ishaque Ali paid the consideration, that defendant No. 2 admitted to be a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali, and the fact that the deeds dated 29-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 in original, Exhibit 1 (c) and Exhibit 1 (d), were produced from the custody of the plaintiffs, the trial Court held that Ishaque Ali purchased said 1.40 acre of land in the 'Benami' of defendant No. 2 Ramendra Nath. Appellate Court just dittoed such finding of the trial Court.

<u>33. Source of the consideration and custody of the deeds may be important circumstances and/or ingredients to prove a transaction 'Benami' but they cannot be taken to be the dominant circumstances. Of course, no hard and fast rule can be prescribed for guidance to decide the question of 'Benami'. Every case of 'Benami' has to be decided having regard to its peculiar facts and circumstances.</u>

<u>34. It is now well settled that besides the source of consideration and custody of document, motive for the transaction, position and relationship between the real owner and ostensible owner i.e. the 'Benamdar', and the conduct dealing with the property are dominant circumstances for the Court to be guided in deciding the question of 'Benarni'. See 34 DLR (AD) 61 and 49 DLR (AD) 73.</u>

35. Here why Ishaque Ali purchased the land in the name of defendant No.2 Ramendra Nath who belonged to a different community has not been explained. PW 1 Raji Haider claimed that defendant No. 2 was their 'Karma chari' At, the time of transaction, he was a mere boy of about nine years only. No other witness was examined to prove that defendant No.2 was a 'Karmachari'. Further, in presence of 10 plaintiffs, who are direct descendants of Ishaque Ali, he cannot be believed to have purchased the land in the name of defendant No. 2. Moreover, during his lifetime, there is no evidence on record that Ishaque Ali ever demanded return of the land from defendant No.2.

In the circumstances and on such evidence on record, concurrence by the appellate Court of the view of the trial Court on the 'Benami' transaction must be held to be not based on any accepted principles of law relating to 'Benami' transaction and cannot be accepted.

36. More I examine respective cases of the parties more I find that fate of the case appears to depend on the factum of possession. Moreover, possession of the suit land including the land claimed to be covered by the 'Benami' transaction, I believe, would make crystal clear not only the case of 'Benami' but also the entire case.

37. Plaintiffs claim that after purchase, Ishaque Ali raised a farm house by raising structures on the land for labours and got the land cultivated by 'Borgadars'. During the season, he used to keep cattle and stay in the farm house for the purpose of cultivation and harvest. In paragraph 11 of the plaint it is categorically averred that in 1394 BS ,the suit 'land was given in 'Borga to defendant No.1. After harvest defendant No. 1 brought the paddy to the farm house of the plaintiffs but did not give 'Borga' share to the plaintiffs. Plaintiffs thereupon constrained to file Case No. 17 of 1988.

38. In his evidence, plaintiff No. 1 as PW 1 said that the suit land was given to defendant No. 1 by his father for 'Borga' cultivation: He further said that defendant No. 1 used to give 'Borga' share of the suit land. Such evidence of PW 1 which is contradictory and beyond the case made out in the plaint should not deserve any consideration. Moreover, it would not be safe, to rely upon PW 1 Raji Haider for his tender age, on the case of possession by Ishaque Ali,

39. One Bimal Krishna Nath claiming to be son of Chintaharan Nath of village Mulagram as PW 2 proved the deed dated 28-12-1972, exhibit 1(a) by which he purchased from Nani Bala Ghoshe and the deed dated 12-4-1973; exhibit 1 by which he transferred 2.89 acres to Ishaque Ali. He however, did not say a word about the possession on the land covered by deed dated 28-12-1972 and 1-4-1974, Exhibit 1(c) and Exhibit 1(d).

What struck me most is that the recipient under the deed dated 28-12-1972, Exhibit-1 (a) is one Bimal Krishna Debnath, son of late Chintaharan Debnath of village Pantadubi. How Bimal Debnath of Pantadubi could examine as PW 2 Birnal Nath of village Mulgram was neither explained nor did attract the attention of any of the Courts below.

40. PW 3 Abdur Rahman deposed that he cultivated the suit land as it 'Borgadar' Defendant No. 1 never possessed the suit land. There was no other house excepting the farm house. He and his son live in the farm house. His evidence does not refer to any time frame and contradicts the case as made out in paragraph 11 of the plaint and PW 5 Fakruddin.

41. PW 4 Abdul Mannan came to prove a 'Chowkidari' tax receipt, exhibit 3 only.

42. PW 5 Fakruddin claimed to be a member of the Union Parishad. He said that there was a farm house in the suit land. Defendant No. 1 cultivated the suit land this year (only) as cultivator. He did not give the 'Borga' produce. CR case No. 17/88 was filed for non-giving and misappropriation of 'Borga' produce.

43. I have already considered hereinabove the deposition of PW 6 Yusuf Ali, who came to prove the deeds dated 28-12-1972 and 12-4-1973. He was no witness to possession by Ishaque Ali followed by 'Benami' transaction.

44. On the other hand, defendant No.2 deposed as DW 1 that his father took 'Pattan' of the suit land along with other land from recorded tenants Indobhushan, Nani Bala, Rebuti Ranjan, Subhasini and Sarala Bala long ago. He could not say how his father took 'Pattan'. His father used to possess the land on the basis of 'Pattan'. His father obtained a decree in Title Suit No. 47 of 1957 in respect of the suit land. In 1968, his father died leaving him as one son and one daughter. He started cultivating the suit land since the death of his father and living in the huts raised. He got the land mutated on the basis of the decree. He paid 'Chowkidari' tax.

45. He also said that the plaintiffs having burnt down his huts, he lodged criminal case against them. In cross, he said that his father cultivated five and half Bigahs of land. He also said that in 1969, Indobhusan and Subhasini went to India forever.

46. DW 2 Dula Rani, aged 53, deposed that she lived in the house made by her father south of the suit land. She said that defendant No. 1 possessed the suit land for many years. She never saw the plaintiffs possessing the suit land. She also deposed on the possession of previous Hindu owners. She said that Indobhushan and Nani Bala went to India 25/26 years ago forever.

47. DW 3 Muktader Ali, aged 41 years, said that defendant No. 1 possessed the suit land by living and cultivation for 18/19 years. Before him his father possessed the suit land. He never saw the plaintiffs or their father possessing the suit land. In cross, he said that he purchased land near the suit land. He heard that defendant No. 1 possessed the suit land as 'Borgadar' of plaintiffs but he never saw that Defendant No. 1 constructed a farm house in the suit land.

48. DW 4 Abdul Mannan Mallik, aged 40 years, deposed that defendant No. 1 lived in the suit land. He cultivated the suit land since before independence. Plaintiffs or their father never possessed the suit land. In cross, he said that the plaintiffs took away the paddy this year. Now, the plaintiffs possess the suit land.

49. DW 5 Abdul Malek Khan, aged about 47 years, deposed that defendant No. 1 cultivates the suit land and lives erecting huts in the house of Indobhusan. He never saw anyone excepting the defendant No.1 possessing the suit land.

50. In support of his case, defendant No.1 also adduced a certified copy of the plaint in Title Suit No. 49 of 1957 filed on 4-2-1957, order dated 28-10-1957 decreeing the suit ex parte and decree drawn. They were marked as Exhibit-A, A (1) and A(3). Certified copies were obtained on 13-3-1980. No doubt could be cast on the authenticity of the certified copies. But the Courts below found that the certified copies were created for the suit.

51. Had genuineness of any of the copies struck the eyes in any way, then who prevented them to verify the copies with the originals which were not far away from them. Moreover, there was no evidence adduced to create any doubt. Rather, it was the case of the plaintiffs that they came to know that the defendant No. 1's father obtained a decree in respect of the suit land. As Corts of fact, lower Courts are required to give decision on proof, not doubt. Any decision based on doubt cannot be binding and/or sustained in revision.

52. The above oral evidence of the parties on possession if compared with the evidence of the defendant No. 1 becomes overwhelming and weightier. The trial Court also could not but accept the possession of defendant No.1. Similarly, findings of the Courts below that defendant No. 1 possessed the suit land on behalf of the plaintiffs as 'Borgadar' and defendant No.2 was a 'Benamdar' of Ishaque Ali, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs in respect of two 'Kabalas' dated 18-12-1972 and 1-4-1974 Exhibits 1(c) and 1(d) are all arbitrary as not based on the evidence on record.

53. Plaintiffs also failed to adduce any decree or any papers of any suit in support of their case that defendant No.4 on compromise in a suit transferred 53.75 decimals to plaintiff Nos. 1 to 7. Defendant No.4 did not even turn up to support the case of the plaintiffs. No explanation was furnished by the plaintiffs for not examining said defendant No.4. Nobody was examined to prove the deed of sale dated 15-8-1987.

<u>54. It may again be remembered that in a suit for declaration of title only production of deeds of purchase without proof of title and possession of their previous owners within twelve years of the suit would not entitle the plaintiff(s) to any decree. The suit would be doomed to fail.</u>

55. But the trial Court appears to have been swayed away when the defendant No. 1 could not say definitely on the 'Pattan' obtained by his father. It reasoned that defendant No. 1 then failed to prove his title. Possession follows title. It forgot to place the burden of proof on right side.

56. The defendant No. 1 did not seek any declaration of title in the suit land. It is the plaintiffs who instituted the suit for declaration of their title in the suit land. Burden was therefore, on them to prove their title. Defendant No. 1 just took the defence that he had title in the suit land on the basis of the decree obtained by his father.

57. In support of the decree, defendant No.1 adduced certified copy of the plaint of Title Suit No. 49 of 1957, entire order sheet of said suit and the decree passed therein. Besides, certified copy' of order sheet of Case No. 4222/1960-61 and Mutation Case No. 9p/1987-88. Decree was passed against Indobhushan, Saralabala, Rabuti Ranjan, Nagendra Nath and others from whom the plaintiffs and their predecessor-in-interest Ishaque Ali claimed title. Such decree was though passed ex parte yet binding upon not only the judgment debtors but also any of their successors-in-interest.

<u>58. The plaintiffs however, did not seek any relief against the decree. Nor did they challenge the decree in the suit. In the context of such suit, the defendant No.1 was not required to prove 'Pattan'. The Courts below therefore fell in serious error in holding against the defendant No.1 for his failure in not adducing evidence on 'Pattan'. Moreover, it must be remembered that long continuous possession for more than statutory period of twelve years has perfected any defect that may be found in the title of defendant No.1 in the suit land and other land possessed by him.</u>

59. For foregoing reasons, the plaintiffs must be held to have failed to prove title and/or possession in the suit land. Finding on possession, however concurrent by the Courts below, being not based on the evidence oral and documentary and law, cannot be binding in revision. The case is very old. So, I had to take pain to find afresh the issues the parties are found to be in variance on the basis of the evidence on record and law.

60. Impugned judgment and decree affirming those of the trial Court therefore, cannot stand in law and cannot be sustained.

61. In the result, the Rule is made absolute with costs. Impugned judgment and decree affirming those of trial Court decreeing the suit are hereby set aside and the suit is dismissed.

Send down the record at once.

End.

caseno: Civil Revision No. 474 of 1991 with Civil Revision No. 475 of 1991
lawyer:
Nikhilesh Dutta with Mihir Kanti Majumder, Advocates ----- For the Petitioners. 
AQM Safiullah with Md Ali Zinnah, Advocates ----- For record.
parties:
Debendra Kumar Saha & another ------ Petitioners
vs
Uttara Bank Ltd ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
These two Rules arise from a common judgment a such this judgment would govern both the Rules.

2. Plaintiff-opposite party filed Title Suit Nos. 396 and 397 of 1981 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Sadar, Noakhali for ejectment of the defendant-petitioners from the suit land on the ground of default and bonafide requirement.

3. The facts of these suits are that the defendant-petitioners were monthly tenants at the rate of Taka 150 under predecessor of the plaintiff Bank in respect of the northern room of the suit premises named as "Singha Brothers Building" along with a four-roofed tin shed, the schedule of the properties is 0.5 decimals of land of plot No . 749 appertaining to DS khatian No: 1103 under Mouja Hajipur, Upazila Begumgonj. This property was auction sold and purchased by Bath Bank Limited on 6-5-1952 in Money Execution Case No. 6 of 1981 of the Court of Subordinate Judge, Noakhali and got delivery of possession on 19-6- 1952. Thereafter, the said Bank converted to Eastern Banking Corporation and thereafter converted to Uttara Bank Limited. After liberation of Bangladesh, the defendant did not pay rents regularly and paid rent up to 1384 BS. Thereafter, they stopped payment of rent and became habitual defaulters. The plaintiff bank requires the suit premises bonafide for opening a new branch at the said premises and the building is required for re-construction and renovation and therefore, the plaintiff terminated the tenancy of the defendant on the expiry of the month of Jaishtha, 1387 BS by serving a notice under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act and asked the defendants to vacate the premises.

4. The defendant-petitioners contested the suit by filing written statement wherein they denied the plaint case and their specific case is that the disputed premises were let out to them on yearly basis from 1950 AD by the then landlord Girish Chandra Singhha at a rental of Taka 750 and as per oral agreement it was a lease for indefinite period and thereafter they became successive tenants under Bath Bank. Eastern Mercantile Bank and thereafter, at present under the Uttara Bank and they regularly paid rents for last 40 years. The rents were subsequently enhanced to Taka 1350 in the year 1374 BS and at that rate also the defendant paid rents regularly up to 1382 BS. In the last part of Chaitra 1383 BS the plaintiff Bank proposed to enhance the rate of rent but payment of rent was not received for want of decision from the Head Office of Uttara Bank. In the year 1384 BS the defendant proposed to re-fix the rents of the premises by a letter to which the plaintiff Bank by Memo No. CMH/OF/FRENT/78-79 dated 12-4-1978 informed that the rent was enhanced to Taka 1800 for the subsequent years. Mr Chandra Shekhar, an employee of the plaintiff Bank, was entrusted for the purpose of collecting rent from the defendants and accordingly, the defendants deposited their rents to Chandra Shekhar for the years 1385 and 1386 BS but no receipt was issued to them by the Bank as it was awaiting approval from the Head Office.

5. It is the further case of the defendants that they received a letter on 15-5-1980 from the plaintiff-Bank in which the Bank denied payment of any rents for the year 1385-1386 BS. The defendants went to the Manager of the local branch of the Bank who could not give any satisfactory reply. On being confronted by the defendants, Chandra Shekhar refunded the money he received from the defendants as rents. They, were asked to act as per law and thereafter the defendants sent Taka 3600 on 23-5-1980 under money order but the said money orders were refused by the plaintiff- Bank. Finding no other alternative the defendants deposited Taka 3600 as rent for the years 1385 and 1386 BS to the rent controller in Rent Control Case No. 1 of 1980. The defendants paying rents regularly in the said case The instant suit is premature because Rent Control Case is still pending. The plaintiff's case having been initiated on false plea, is liable to be dismissed with costs.

6. On these pleadings the learned Assistant Judge framed four issues namely, issue No. 1 relating to maintainability of the suit, issue No. 2 relating to valuation of the suit, issue No.3 relating to relief as prayed for and issue No.4 relating to what other relief plaintiff is entitled to.

7. On consideration of the depositions and documentary evidences on record, the learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 21-10-1989 dismissed the suit holding that the defendants are not defaulter, the tenancy is on yearly basis and the plaintiff fails to prove bonafide requirement. On the other hand, the learned District Judge in Title Appeal Nos. 187 and 188 of 1989 preferred by the plaintiff-Bank allowed the appeals and decreed the suit holding that in absence of any registered document, the tenancy is to be treated as monthly tenancy and the defendants are habitual defaulters in paying rents. Learned Judge further held that for installing a new branch the plaintiff required the suit premises bonafide.

8. Mr Nikhilesh Dutta with Mr Mihir Kanti Majumder, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the defendant-petitioners, submits that the Court of appeal below committed gross illegality is holding that the tenancy is monthly one without considering that the defendants are paying rents regularly for the last 40 years on yearly basis. He further submits that the plaintiffs failed to prove that the suit premises is required by them bonafide but the learned District Judge, as a final Court of fact, decreed the suit on that score. In support of their contention, the learned Advocate gave much emphasis on Exhibit B.

9. Mr AQM Shafiullah, the learned Advocate for the plaintiffs-opposite party submits that the Court of appeal below on the facts of the given case committed no illegality in holding that in absence of any registered instrument tenancy is monthly one. He further submits that if Exhibit B is read properly it would appear merely as a letter of information but not an agreement for lease.

10. To answer the submissions of the learned Advocates and to arrive at the finding whether the learned District Judge committed illegality in decreeing the suit, I am to consider the depositions led by the parties and exhibits filed by them.

11. The defendant's case is that, they paid rents for the years 1385-1386 BS to one Chandra Shekhar who was entrusted by the Bank to collect rents from the defendants. It is their own averments that Chandra Shekhar did not deposit the rents to the Bank. To prove their case that they paid rents to Chandra Shekhar and, as such, they are not defaulters, the defendants could examine Chandra Shekhar but they did not. Since Chandra Shekhar was not examined the defendants on their own admission become defaulter in paying rents for the year of 1385-1386 BS. Having confronted with such factual aspect the learned Advocates for the petitioners gave up' their claim that the defendants are not defaulter in paying rents. The defendants could be evicted from the suit premises on this finding alone that they are defaulter. Anyone of the two requirements (defaulter and bonafide requirement), if proved, is sufficient to evict a tenant.

12. To prove whether the tenancy was a monthly one or on yearly basis, learned Advocate for the petitioners gave much emphasis on Exhibit B. To appreciate the submission of the learned Advocate, Exhibit B is quoted here. It started as Memo No. CHM/OF RENT/78/97 dated 12-4-1978. I find that it is addressed to defendant. "M/s. Satya Narayan Stores, .Singha Brothers Building, Chaumuhani, Noakhali." and it started addressing "Dear Sir", Then subject matter was given as "Enhancement of rent of southern portion of Singha Brothers Building". Then it was written as; "With reference to your petition dated 2-1- 83 BS we have the pleasure to inform you that the management have been pleased to fix up the temporary yearly rent of southern portion of Signha Brothers Building possessed by you at Taka 1,800 (Taka one thousand eight hundred) only with effect from 1st Baishakh 1384 BS provided that all sorts of repairing and renovation works of your portion of the building are done at your own cost under the supervision of the undersigned". Thereafter, this exhibit concluded as; "Meanwhile, you are further advised to clear up the arrear rent of the building at the new rate first, then after completion of repairing works you are advised to come forward to execute a lease agreement with us at an early date."

13. The statements "temporary yearly rent" and "you are advised to come forward to execute a lease agreement" are noticeable. These statements prove that although the plaintiff has taken the defendants as temporary yearly tenant but no agreement was made to that effect.

On reading of Exhibit "B", I find that this Exhibit B is a letter intimating the intention of the plaintiff accepting the defendants as tenant on condition of payment of their arrear rents and on repairing the building. But most important thing is that this letter contains if the defendants have performed some conditions then they would execute a lease agreement. From depositions of the witnesses as well as averments made by the defendants in the written statement, I find that they 'did not come forward to execute a lease deed because they failed' to fulfill the conditions. If assuming that this letter gave the defendants the intention of the plaintiff that they would continue as yearly tenant but find that such 'intention of the plaintiffs not accessible to any law. A letter cannot be construed to be 'an agreement Letter' bears only' information but agreement is the product of the settlement of the disagreement of the parties wherein signatures of the parties to the dispute with witnesses is a must. Letters reflects the mind of its writer but agreement is product of resolving dispute. Section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act speaks that "in absence of contract or local law of usage to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for agricultural or manufacturing purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from year to year, terminable, on the part of either lessor or lessee, by six months notice expiring with the end of a year of the tenancy; and a lease of immovable property for any other purpose shall be deemed to be a lease from month to month terminable on the part of either lessor or lesse by fifteen days notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

Section 107 of the said Act speaks that;

A lease of immovable property from year to year or for any term exceeding one year, or preserving a yearly rent, can be made only by a registered instrument."

<u>14. The learned Advocate for the petitioners submits that since the defendants have been treated by previous landlord and by present landlord as a tenant on yearly basis, notice under section 106 of the said Act, is incompetent but from the pleadings of the defendant I find no registered instrument have been executed by either parties qualifying the tenancy as yearly one. In absence of any registered documents the claim of the defendants-petitioners that they have had been treated as tenant on yearly basis is of no substance. I am supported by 43 CWN 797, 22 DLR 56, 22 DLR (SC) 360 and 1987 BLD (AD) 147. In the decision reported in 43 CWN 797 it has been held that;</u>

<u>"If any lessee enters into possession on the basis of an oral agreement, without any period, being fixed for the lease, and continues in possession on payment of rent to the lessor, the lease, when the purpose is neither agricultural nor manufacturing, must be taken to be a lease from month to month under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act."</u>

<u>In the decision reported in 22 DLR 56 it has been held that;</u>

<u>"Tenant continued in possession in absence of renewal of the original lease or further agreement and the landlord accepted the rent- holding over of such premises by the tenant will be governed not by the original lease but by the general provisions of section 106 of the Act."</u>

<u>In the decision reported in 22 DLR (SC) 360 it has been held that;</u>

<u>Unregistered lease deed of immovable property from year to year is inadmissible in evidence for lack of registration."</u>

<u>In the decision reported in 1987 BLD(AD) 147 it has been held that;</u>

<u>"Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act provides that a lease of immovable property for a period exceeding one year can be made only by a registered instrument. This implies that a lease for a period not exceed one year may be made by an unregistered instrument. Even if a lease is created for a longer period by an unregistered instrument it will be valid only for one year.</u>

<u>15. I find that the sheet anchor of the defendants in support of their case that they are yearly tenant is Exhibit "B" and from reading of Exhibit "B" I find it is merely a letter disclosing the intention of the plaintiff-Bank. But in absence of any registered deed of agreement I cannot but find the defendants are tenants at will terminable by notice of 15 days. The principle of terminating tenancy rests primarily on two conditions-one is defaulter and another is bonafide requirement. Existence of anyone of these two conditions is suffice to eject a tenant. From their own averments the defendants are habitual defaulters for not paying rents for the year 1385-1386 BS. The Court of appeal below further found that the suit premises is required by the plaintiff-Bank for installing a branch at the suit premises. This being a finding of facts by the Court of appeal below, which is the final Court on a matter of fact, is binding upon this Court in Revisional Jurisdiction. I find no substance in both these Rules.</u>

In the result, both the Rules are discharged. No cost.

Send down the lower Court records.

End.

caseno: First Appeal No. 216 of 2007 with Civil Rule No. 497 (f) of 2007.
lawyer:
Jamiruddin Sirker with AHM Mushfiqur Rahman, Advocates----- For the Appellants.
A Baset Majumder, with Abdul Barik Chowdhur, Advocates----- For the Respondents.
parties:
Momena Khatun and others ----- Appellants
Vs.
Hussain Fabrics Ltd. And others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Sharifuddin Chaklader J : This appeal by the plaintiffs, directed against Judgment and Decree dated 19-6-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, Arbitration Adalat, Dhaka dismissing Title Suit No. 102 of 2004 for Specific Performance or Contract.

2. Appellants who are plaintiffs, stated ill the plaint, that RAJUK plot No. 12, Factory Road. Shyampur Kadamtali Industrial Area allotted to defendant No. 1, a private limited company under Companies Act vide memo dated 30-7-1985. or whom, Kazi Golam Hussain was the Chairman and other members of his family are directors includiIlg Kazi Zahir Hussain, who was the Managing Director, having in need of money the Board of Directors of defendant No. 1 on 3-10-1989 decided to sell suit property and expressed their desire to that effect, to which, AI-haj Mansur Rahman, predecessor of the plaintiffs agreed to purchase and price was settled at Taka 34,50,000. On 19-3-1990, plaintiffs paid Taka 18,50,000 through cheque, as earnest money in presence of witnesses. Consequently, a written agreement in respect of the suit property in favour of the predecessor of plaintiff on certain tenns and conditions was executed in bainapatra dated 19-3-1990 and thereafter, defendant No. 1 delivered physical possession of the suit plot to the plaintiffs. Defendant No. 1 wrote a letter to the Managing Director of Uttara Bank Ltd on 16-9-1990, in which admitted the agreement for sale dated 19-3-1990 and also admitted possession of the plaintiffs. Defendant No.1 due to financial problem, failed to pay installments to RAJUK, as such, some dispute arose between RAJUK and defendant No. 1 and defendant No. 1 requested the plaintiffs to take responsibility for payment of the entire installments to which the predecessor of the plaintiffs agreed and plaintiffs at first paid some installments in total Taka 19 lacks and Taka 14 lacks were remain unpaid. Plaintiffs also made payment to RAJUK the entire installments. The predecessor of the plaintiffs, thereafter requested the defendants to execute and register the sale deed, to which, defendant Nos. 2 to 4 and Kazi Golam Hussain executed a security bond on 18-3-1992 admitting the agreement for sale dated 19-3-1990. It is further plaint case that Kazi Golam Hossain, Chairman of defendant No. 1 and predecessor of defendant Nos. 2 to 4 handed over the original lease deed to the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs in respect of the suit property with the assurance to execute and register the sale deed. Meanwhile Kazi Golam Hossain died leaving behind defendant Nos. 2 to 4 as his heirs, who are also directors of defendant No. 1 After he death Kazi Golam Hossain, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, AI- Haj Mansur Rahman requested the principal defendants to execute and register the sale deed to which at first they agreed but later on, step aside. In the meantime, on 20-11-1998, the predecessor of the plaintiffs died. Thereafter plaintiffs requested principal defendants to execute and register the sale deed but defendant Nos. 1 and 2 with the help or some local mastans and political touts, threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs and abused them with filthy language to which plaintiff No.2 made GD entry No. 259 dated 20-6-2000 with the Shyampur Police Station. On 21-12-2001 defendant No. 2 with the help of some local mastans, forcibly and illegally trespassed in to the suit premises and mercilessly beaten the care taker and darwan of the plaintiffs and took away valuable articles from their quarter and thereafter, left the place, for which, plaintiff No. 2 lodged an FIR with Shyampur police station and accordingly Shyampur PS Case No. 32(12) 2001 under section 323/448/143/427/380/506 of the penal Code was started and subsequently. charge sheet was submitted. Defendant No.2 also tiled a case under section 145 CrPC being Case No. 5877 or 2001 before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate over which, learned Chief Metropolitan Magistrate called report from Officer-in-Charge, Shyampur Police Station. Officer-in-Charge, Shyampur Police Stat ion submitted report. Thereafter, plaintiff applied to the Officer-in-Charge, Shyampur Police Station for posting 10 Ansars with fire arms and the application ultimately was allowed by the Commissioner or Metropolitan of Police vide memo dated 19-1-2002. Finally 10 Ansars along with fire arms were posted in the mill with a direction to the plaintiff No. 2 to bear their salary and ration vide memo No. 4127 dated 20-1-2002. Plaintiffs have been paying the same regularly. And thereafter when the defendants totally refused to execute and register the sale deed the suit was filed.

3. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 filed written statements denying the case of the plaintiffs. The defendants did not examine any witness in support or the case made out in the written statement. Since they did not examine any witness in favour of the written statement we are not require to consider that case but for effective disposal of the appeal, the relevant portion of their written statement is required to be mentioned.

4. The defendants did not denied he fact that the suit property was allotted by DIT/RAJUK to Messrs Hussain Fabrics Ltd. defendant No. 1 but they have denied the Chairman has authority to deal with the property. It is their case that Kazi Golam Hossain was the father of the defendant No.2, had a intimacy with Mansur Rahman, the predecessor of the plaintiffs who was the owner of Hotel Al Mansur situated at Gulistan, Dhaka. Said Mansur Rahman was successful in derailing Kazi Golam Hussain by provogating him with loose character women and wine. Kazi Golam Hussain then used to pass his maximum time in the said hotel and it be came the sweet home of illicit relation of Kazi Golam Hossain with lady of immoral character to which defendant No. 2 while came to know about the demoralization of Kazi Golam Hossain, protested to Mr Mansur Rahman and there was a family quarrel over this matter and at one stage, the younger brother of defendant No.2 shot the wife of defendant No. 2 and killed her on the spot. While Kazi Golam Hussain was in affairs with Mansur Rahman to grab the property of these defendants, managed to obtain a deed of agreement executed by Kazi Ghulam Hossain alleging that he was the Chairman of Messrs Hussain Fabrics. Actually Kazi Golam Hossain has no authority to deal with the affairs of Messrs Hussain Fabrics Ltd. On 18-3-1992 plaintiff No.3 with the help of some gunda elements came to the residence of the defendants and placed a security bond and was forced the defendants to execute. After the death of Mansur Rahman, plaintiff No.2 submitted various documents in different offices where from this defendant came to learn that the security bond obtained by Mahbubur Rahman in respect of the suit property, not in respect of the property of Messrs Hussain Fabrics. This defendant did not deny the fact that Ansars were posted by the plaintiff. Defendant No.2 filed Writ Petition 242 of 2002 before the Hon'ble Court Division and obtained the order of injunction. Defendant also filed petition Case No. 5877 of 2001 before the Court of Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka wherein order of maintaining status quo was passed. But plaintiff with the help of some gunda clements, and by violating the order of injunction or the Hon'ble High Court Division, entered into suit premises and Contempt Petition No.9 of 2002 was filed before the High Court Division and rule was issued which is pending. Thereafter submitted that there is no contract for selling of the suit property.

5. At the trial plaintiffs examined 4 witnesses and defendant examined no witness.

6. Plaintiff exhibited a number of document- i.e. power of attorney dated 26-1-2002, as exhibit I. allotment letter dated 30-7-85 in favour of defendant No.1, as exhibit 2, deed of agreement (bainapatra) dated 19-3-1990 and signature of witness No. 2 Belal Hossain, as exhibit Nos. 3 and 3ka. Certificate dated 26-8-1990 issued by City Bank acknowledgement receipt of money as exhibit No.4. Document relating handing over the materials and signatures or witness Md Belal Hossain as exhibit Nos. 5 and Ska. Application to the Managing Director Uttara Bank dated 16-9-1990 as exhibit No.6. Modified deed or agreement dated 23-9-1990 and signature of witness No.3 as exhibit Nos. 7 and 7/1.Deposit of Taka 14,29,303 by pay Order, Cheque and Challan as exhibits Nos. 8 to 8(chha). Security Bond dated 18-3-1992 as exhibit No.9 Lease Deed No. 5175 dated 9-8-92 exhibit No. 10. Letters dated 10-7-1998. 26-7-1998 and 5-8-1998 as exhibit Nos. 11 to 11 kha. GD Entry No. 1259 dated 20-6=2000 as exhihit No. 12 FIR in Shyampur PS Case No. 32(12) 01 as exhibit No. 13. Order sheet, Petition and Police report in Petition Case No. 5877/01of Court or Chief Metropolitan Magistrate as exhibit Nos. 14 to 14(kha) Order of appointment of Ansars dated 20-1- 2002 and receipts of payment of money as exhibit . Nos. 15 to 15 (jha). Return of allotment dated 15-6-1987 to the Registrar, Joint Stock Companies as exhibit No. 16 Plaint in Title Suit No.1 of 1994 of the 4th Artha Rin Adalat. Dhaka as exhibit No. 17.Certified Copy of Vokalatnama in Title Suit No.1 or 1994 as exhibit No. 18 and Written Statement in Title Suit No.1 of 1994, and meeting of Board of Directors of Hussain Fabrics Ltd. dated 3-10-1989 as exhibit 19 and 20.

7. Learned Judge dismissed the suit, Learned Judge while dismissing the suit found that admittedly the suit property was the property of Messrs Hussain Fabrics Ltd. But learned Judge held that plaintiff is to prove the fact that Kazi Golam Hossain was the Chairman of defendant No. 1 and held that since plaintiff failed to produce the Memorandum and Article of Association of the Company, the fact that Kazi Golam Hossain was the Chairman of defendant No. 1 has not been proved. Learned Judge on the possession of the suit property by plaintiffs held that such possession of the plaintiffs are on using muscle men, mastans and with the help of political leaders in power and got possession of the suit property forcibly dispossessing the defendants and thereafter, dismissed the suit.

8. Mr Jamiruddin Sirker, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-appellants, submits that, learned Judge misread the evidence and thereafter wrongly held that plaintiffs is to prove that Kazi Golam Hussain, the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 2 and 3 was the Chairman of the defendant No. 1 as the plaintiff did not produce the memorandum and article of association of defendant No. 1. Learned Advocate further submits that, plaintiff is no way connected with defendant No. 1 and memorandum and article of association is not a book which can be procured from the book stall or foot- path to be produced by plaintiffs in Court in prove the fact that Kazi Golam Hossain was the Chairman of defendant No.1. On the question of possession by the plaintiffs learned Advocate submits that plaintiff through natural and neutral witness and by documentary evidence proved the execution of bainapatra and pursuant to that bainapatra plaintiff was inducted into possession by original owner of the suit property. Here learned Advocate submits that original documents in favour of the original allottee having been produced from the side of the plaintiff proves the fact that plaintiffs were inducted into possession by the original allottee not through mastans. Learned Advocate further submits that, since defendant did not examine any witness learned Judge acted beyond his jurisdiction in considering the written statement filed by the defendants.

9. On the other hand Mr A Baset Majumder, learned Advocate with Mr Abdul Barik Chowdhury learned Advocate, appearing for the defendant- respondents, submits that, defendants although did not adduce any witness or did not produce any documents but the fact remains that defendants' predecessor was the original allottee and also submit that they did not produce any document and adduced any witness before the Court as at the relevant time and situation was difficult and also defendants were threatened with dire consequence by the party from appearing in Court and to depose. Learned Advocate refer some orders of the learned Joint District Judge to prove the situation prevailing at the relevant time. Learned Advocate further submits by filling an application under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure that the judgment is not good to he maintained as such defendants may be given a chance of prove their case by adducing evidence oral and documentary annexed with the application by sending the suit back on remand.

10. At first we are very sorry to mention that the learned Judge delivered the judgment not in accordance with law. The plaintiffs in order to prove their case produces before the Court number of documents including original documents and also established their case through natural witness who deposed in their favour, Learned Judge kept a blind eye to the evidence of the plaintiffs and was of the opinion the since plaintiffs fail to produce the memorandum and article of association to prove the tact that the defendants predecessor was actually Chairman of defendant No. 1 the bainapatra cannot be treated as proper document to be enforceable under law. We are sorry to mention here that learned judge probably had not read the Evidence Act. particularly section 102 and 102 where the law is that the person who alleged certain fact he is to prove such fact. To prove Kazi Golam Hossain was not Chairman of the defendant No. 1, onus squarely lies on the defendants to discharged such onus as they raised the question. Defendant in order to prove Kazi Golam Hossain was not Chairman of defendant No. 1 ought to lead evidence to that effect and in order to prove that fact, it is the defendants who is required to produce the company s document including Memorandum and Article of Association of defendant No. 1. It appears that defendants did not discharge the onus as they did not adduce any witness nor produce any document.

<u>11. Learned Judge found possession of the plaintiffs but held that plaintiffs got possession through musclemen, and this finding was solely on consideration of written statement but this fact has not been borne out by the defendants as they did not examine any witness. It appears that the original documents of the suit property came from the custody of the plaintiffs.</u>

12. On the question of additional evidence, Mr A Baset Majurnder, learned Advocate argued that due to political situation at the relevant time defendants were not able to go to the Court and did not produce the evidence before the Court and referred certain orders. It is true that time there was some difficulties in enjoyment day to day life. But we find from the lower Court records that all the applications filed by defendants for adjournment of the proceedings of the suit were made either for illness of the witnesses or illness of the learned Advocate or learned Advocate was busy in some other Court and was unable to appear before the Court, not a single application was filed to show that due to threatened of the plaintiffs defendants failed to appear before the Court.

13. Relief for specific performance of a con- tract is a discretionary relief. In granting such relief Court along with law and fact, also consider the nature, conduct and attitude of the parties. In the case in hand defendants who are sons of Kazi Golam Hossain, in order to deny the contract, branded him as:-

"Mr Mansur Rahman became successful in derailing Kazi Golam Hossain by provocating with the help of prostitute women and wine, Kazi Golam Hossain then used to pass his maximum time in the said Hotel and it was became the sweet home of illicit relation of Kazi Golam Hossain with lady of immoral character. Human being are selfish and cruel. For the survival human being can do anything and cruelty go beyond imagination. When anyone's self interest effected then the act of human being go beyond imagination and to protect self interest even one can murder his/ her own child. But it is too much to consume when we see the own son of deceased father branded father as debauched which the defendants in their written statement characterized their father."

14. On the question of additional evidence, Let us refer Order XLI rule 27 of the Code of Civil Procedure which gives two precondition for accepting additional evidence, of them, one in that. if the parties who sought for adducing additional evidence was refused by the Court to admit such evidence then his evidence can be brought into consideration as additional evidence and next, when the appellate Court required such documents. Moreover in accepting the additional evidence it is to he seen whether these document were in possession of the parties when the trial was held and it appears that these documents were in custody of the defendants but they did not produce before the trial Court as such, now to till up the lacuna, prayed the cast: be sent back on remand to the trial Court which no Court could subscribe.

15. We find substance in his appeal.

16. In the result, this appeal is allowed. No costs.

17. The Judgment and decree dated 19-6-2007 passed by the learned Joint District Judge. Arbitration Adalat, Dhaka in Title Suit No. 102 of 2004 is set aside. The suit is decreed.

18. Defendant Nos. 1 and 2 are directed to execute and register the sale deed pursuant to the agreement dated 19-3-1990 within sixty days from the date of receipt of this judgment by the learned Joint Division Judge, failing which the plaintiff is entitled to execute and register the sale deed through Court in accordance with law.

Connected Civil Rule No. 457(f) of 2007 is made absolute.

The order of injunction granted earlier at the time of issuance of rule is here by vacated.

Communicate this order at once.

Sent down the lower Court records at once.

End.

lawyer:
JN Dev with Khair-un-nessa,Fouzia Afrin and Chanchal Kumar Biswas Advocates------ For the Petitioner. 
No one appears------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Abul Kashem-al-Asad ------ Petitioner 
vs 
Abdul Muhib and others ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
MA Wahhab Miah J : This Rule was issued calling upon opposite parties No. 1-6 to show cause as to why the orders dated 17-4-2002 and 17-4-2003 passed by the Joint District Judge, Second Court, Sylhet in Title Suit No. 22 of 1998 should not be set aside and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.

2. Opposite parties’ No. 1-6 as plaintiffs filed the said Suit in the Court of Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for partition impleading the present petitioner as defendant No. 1 along with others. It appears that the plaintiffs claimed their saham in the suit land to the extent of 1/8th share from two plots being No. 7080 and 7102 of Chhapa Khatian No. 3159 (ছাপা খতিয়ান) through one Abdus Sobhan as their predecessor-in-interest on declaration of their title. In the said suit the present petitioner appeared and filed an application under Order VII, rule II along with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (the Code) for rejection of the plaint on the ground that previously one Rokeya Banu and others as plaintiffs filed partition Suit No. 206 of 1970 in the same Court impleading Abdus Sobhan, the predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiffs along with others as defendants for partition of the estate of Hajee Abdur Rahman, the predecessor-in-interest of both the plaintiffs and the defendants. Further the present plaintiffs got themselves added in the said Suit as defendants Nos. 8-13 claiming to be the heirs of late Abdus Sobhan and filed written statement. In the said Suit saham was given to Abdus Sobhan who was defendant No. 2 and after his death present defendants Nos. 1 and 2 filed application for substituting them in his place and accordingly, they were substituted as defendants No. 2(ka) and 2 (kha) and the share allotted to said Abdus Sobhan was allotted to them. After the Suit was decreed in preliminary form on 27-12-73 final decree was passed on 29-5- 98 on the basis of the commissioner's report submit- ted on 7-4-88. In the application it was further stated that in the said partition Suit the present plaintiffs filed an application praying for giving them saham of the share of Abdus Sobhan but the court by its order dated 20-12-1988 rejected the prayer. Against the said rejection of their prayer for saham as well as the final decree respectively the plaintiffs did neither file any appeal nor moved the higher court, therefore, the instant Suit filed by them in respect of the self-same Suit property after long time was barred by limitation and the plaint was liable to be rejected.

3. Subordinate Judge by his order dated 17-4- 2002 rejected the said application on the finding as under:

........... শুনিলাম বিবাদীর দাখিলী দরখাস্ত পর্যালোচনা করিয়া দেখিলাম। বিবাদীর দাখিলী দরখাস্ত আর্জি প্রত্যাখানের নিমিত্তে উল্লেখিত কারণ যথাযথ বলিয়া প্রতীয়মান হয় না। অধিকন্তু আর্জি দৃষ্টে আপাতঃ কোন আইন অনুসারে মামলাটি বারিত বলেও প্রতীয়মান হয় না। তাই আর্জি খারিজের প্রার্থনা না মঞ্জুর হইল। আগামী ৮-৫-২০০২ ইং তারিখ বিচার্য বিষয় গঠনের জন্য রহিল।”

4. Thereafter on 28-4-2002 defendant No. I petitioner filed an application under section 151 of the Code for reviewing the order dated 17-4-2002. The learned Joint District Judge by his order dated 17-4-2003 rejected the said application on the view that the previous application was rejected by giving reason, so there was no scope to review the said order. The learned Joint District Judge further observed that if the defendant felt aggrieved by the previous order he could move the higher court. In the revision both the said orders having been impugned Rule was issued accordingly. In the revision application it has been asserted that although the hearing of the said review application took place on 29-8-2002 the court below passed the order rejecting the same after about 8(eight) months.

5. Mr JN Dev, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has taken us through the various annexures which are the copies of the plaint of Partition Suit No. 22 of 1998 (the present suit) the application filed by Abul Kalam Azad and Abul Kashem-al-Asad substituted defendants No. 2(ka) and 2(kha) of the previous Suit for separate saham of 3 annas, 15 gondas and 22/9 donties which was allotted to late Abdus Sobhan, their father, order dated 5-1-1982 passed in Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 allowing their prayer for saham, order dated 20-12- 88 rejecting the prayer for saham of the present plaintiffs who got them impleaded in the previous Suit as defendants Nos. 8- I 3 the report of the Advocate Commissioner dated 3-4-88 which formed part of the final decree, the final decree passed on 29-5- 88 in Title (Partition) Suit No. 206 of 1970 other reports of the Advocate Commissioner submitted on various dates, writ of execution of the decree, firstly of the documents filed before the court below on 8- 5-82 in support of the application for rejection of the plaint. Mr  Dev submits that the documents as annexed to application which were filed before the court below clearly show that the two Suit plots about which partition has been sought for in the present Suit were very much the subject matter of the previous Suit for partition and the prayer of he present plaintiffs to get saham from the said two plots having been rejected on 20-12-88 and the parties having been put into possession of their respective saham pursuant to the final decree passed in the previous Suit there is no scope of re-opening the matter so, the instant suit is clearly barred by the principle of res judicata within the meaning of section 11 of the Code and, as such, the plaint was liable to be rejected, but the learned Joint District Judge failed to consider the apparent facts as stated in the application for rejection of the plaint which were supported by the documents filed before him by firisty and thus committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure of justice in passing the impugned orders and, as such, the same are liable to be set aside and the plaint by rejected.

6. The opposite parties have not entered appearance to oppose the Rule.

7. From the final decree passed in Title Suit (partition) No 206 of 1970 it appears that the suit plots being No. 7080 and 7120 were the subject matter of the previous Suit. From the decree it further appeared that the present plaintiffs were impleaded in the previous Suit as defendants Nos. 8-13. From the order dated 20-12-1988 it is apparent that the prayer of the present plaintiffs to give them saham of the share of late Abdus Sobhan who was given saham in the preliminary decree was rejected. From the order dated 5-1-82 it is also apparent that after the death of Abdus Sobhan who was defendant No. 2 in the previous Suit his share was allotted to the substituted defendants No. 2(ka) and 2(kha) that is present defendants Nos. 1 and 2. In the application for rejection of the plaint those facts were categorically stated but were not denied by the plaintiffs by filing any written objection. From the Firisty vide Annexure-'N' to the revision application it further appeared that the documents as mentioned hereinbefore were filed, but from the impugned order it does not appear that the court below considered those. Before this court also the plaintiff- opposite parties have not appeared and denied the fact by filing any counter-affidavit that the two Suit plots for the partition of which the instant Suit has been filed were the subject matter of the previous Suit. From the plaint of the instant Suit it is also apparent that the plaintiffs suppressed the fact that in the previous Suit they after being impleaded as defendants Nos. 8-13 prayed for giving them saham of the share allotted to Abdus Sobhan in the preliminary decree claiming to be his heirs and that final decree was passed giving saham of said Abdus Sobhan to the two sons as defendants No. 2(ka) and 2(kha), that is the present defendants Nos. 1 and 2, and accordingly, final decree was passed. As the plaintiffs have not denied the assertions made in the application filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code that they neither filed appeal against the final decree passed in the previous Suit nor moved the higher court against the rejection of their prayer for allotting them the saham of late Abdus Sobhan we cannot but accept the submission of Mr JN Dev, that the instant Suit being barred under the provisions of section 11 of the Code of the plaint is liable to be rejected.

<u>8. The learned Subordinate Judge rejected the application for rejection of the plaint on the ground that no law was mentioned under which the plaint was liable to be rejected. The learned Joint District Judge failed to consider that from the facts as stated in the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code it was clear that the Suit was barred by the provisions of section 11 of the Code, as there being already partition of the land previously by metes and bounds in Title Suit No. 206 of 1970 between the parties there was no scope of re-opening the matter again by declaring their title to the portion in the Suit land as claimed by them. It is true that in some cases it may so happen that without taking evidence it may not be possible to decide the question as to when a Suit is barred by the principle of res judicata. But in the instant case the facts as asserted in the application filed under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code that the same Suit plots were the subject matter of the previous partition Suit wherein the present plaintiffs were very much parties and their prayer for saham as the heirs of late Abdus Sobhan was rejected and the decree passed in the earlier Suit was executed and the relevant papers also having been filed by a firisty which the plaintiff did not deny no further evidence was necessary to come to the decision that the suit was barred under the principle of res judicata, so the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in rejecting the application filed by the defendant/ petitioner under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code. In this regard we like to observe that by now it is a well settled legal proposition that in considering an application or a prayer made by a party the court will see the contents of the application and it can give a relief under the appropriate law even if a wrong provision of law is quoted or mentioned, so, the learned Subordinate Judge was wrong in rejecting the application for rejection of the plaint on the view that no provision of law was mentioned under which the suit was barred.</u>

9. For the discussion made above, we are constrained to hold that the court below committed error of law resulting in an error occasioning failure or justice in passing the impugned orders rejecting the application filed by the petitioner under Order VII, rule 11 and section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure and thus in not re-reefing the plaint.

10. In the result this Rule is made absolute. The impugned orders are set aside the plaint of Title (Partition) No. 22 of 1998 of the Court of Joint District Judge Second Court, Sylhet is rejected.

11. No order as to costs.

Communicate the order at once.

End.

lawyer:
Md Abdul Haque. Advocate-For the Petitioner. 
No one appears-For the Opposite Party
parties:
Dr Ahmed Majid ------ Petitioner
vs
Abdul Latif @ Suruj Ali ------ Opposite Party
full_judgment:
This Civil Revision under section 25 of the Small Cause Courts Act, 1987 is about the legality of order dated 24-10-2001 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge and the Court of Small Causes, Sadar, Mymensingh in Small Causes Court Suit No. 13 of 2000.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule are as under.

3. The petitioner as plaintiff instituted Small Causes Court suit No. 13 of 2000 (hereinafter referred to as the SCC suit) in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge and the Court of Small Causes. Sadar, Mymensingh for eviction of his monthly tenant, the defendant opposite party, from the suit premises as described in the plaint on the ground of default in payment of monthly rent. The defendant- opposite party appeared in the suit on 10-1-2001 and prayed for time for filing written statement. Subsequently, the defendant-opposite party took time for filing written statement on 15-3-2001, 2-4-2001 and 13-3-2001. Thereafter, on 21-6-2001 the defendant opposite party submitted an application under section 10 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereafter referred to as the Code) for staying further proceeding of the suit. The plaintiff-petitioner submitted written objection dated 21-6-2001 against the same. Then on 24-10-2001 after hearing the parties, the learned Judge of the Court of Small Causes stayed further proceedings of the SCC suit till disposal of the Partition Suit No. 8 of 1999 which was pending before the Court of the  Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sadar, Mymensingh. It has been stated that the Court below committed an error of law in staying further proceeding of the SCC suit on the ground of a partition suit pending between the parties and others occasioning miscarriage of justice.

4. Noone appears on behalf of the opposite party to oppose the Rule.

5. Mr Md Abdul Hoque, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner, contends that the Court below failed to appreciate that the issues to be decided in a partition suit and the issues to be decided in a SCC suit are completely different. He further contends that in a SCC Suit the issues are mainly whether the relationship of landlord and tenant exists between the parties, whether the tenant is a defaulter in payment of rent, etc., which cannot be decided in a Partition Suit. He lastly contends that the Court below upon misconception of law most erroneously passed the impugned order dated 24-10-2001 which is liable to be set aside.

6. It appears from the certified copy of the plaint of the SCC suit (Annexure-A) that the plaintiff-petitioner filed the said suit against Mr Abdul Latif alias Suruj Ali for his eviction as a monthly tenant on the ground of default in payment of rent since October, 1998. It has been clearly stated in the plaint that defendant-opposite party is a monthly tenant under the plaintiff petitioner at a monthly rental of Taka 70. It further appears from the certified copy of the impugned order of the SCC Suit that the defendant took time on several occasions to file written statement but without filing the same he on 21-6-2001 filed an application under section 10 read with section 151 of the Code for staying the SCC suit. This application (Annexure- B) shows that the defendant-opposite party as plaintiff had filed a Partition Suit against the plaintiff of the SCC suit and of others and the suit premises is also included in the schedule of the partition suit. It has not been denied in this application that the defendant is not a tenant under the plaintiff of the SCC Suit. It appears from the objection (Annexure-C) submitted by the plaintiff-petitioner that he claimed that the defendant is a monthly tenant under him and he has many rent receipts showing that the defendant paid monthly rent to him and the SCC suit cannot be stayed on the ground of a Partition Suit.

7. While passing the impugned order the Court below observed that Partition Suit No. 8 of 1999 is pending before the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, that the suit premises is also included in the schedule of the partition suit and that there is scope for deciding as to whether the defendant is a monthly tenant under the plaintiff in the partition suit and allowed the prayer of defendant and stayed the SCC suit till disposal of the Partition Suit No.8 of 1999.

8. Section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure provides that no Court shall proceed with the trial of any suit in which the matter in issue is also directly and substantially in issue in a previously instituted suit between the same parties, or between parties under whom they or any of them claim litigating under the same title whether such suit is pending in the same or any other Court in Bangladesh having jurisdiction to grant the relief claimed, or in any court beyond the limits of Bangladesh established or continued by the Government and having like jurisdiction, or before the Supreme Court.

<u>9. A Partition Suit is generally filed against the co-sharer and the issues to be decided in such a suit are mainly if a person is a co-sharer of a Khatian the shares of the parties claiming saham, etc., whereas the issues in a SCC suit are whether the relationship. of landlord and the, tenant exists between the parties. Whether a tenant defaulted in payment of rent etc. Even a co-sharer can Jet out his portion of properties to another co-sharer as a monthly tenant. There is no scope for deciding the issues regarding the relationship of .landlord and tenant between the parties, default in payment of rent, etc. in a suit for partition. The Court below failed. to appreciate this legal aspect of the case in accordance with section 10 read with section 151 of the Code and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice.</u>

10. In view of the above, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned order dated 24-10-2001 passed by the Court of Small Causes in SCC suit  No. 13 of 2000 is hereby set aside and the Court is directed to proceed with the suit in accordance with law. No costs.

Communicate the order to the Court below at once.

End.

lawyer:
Mahmudul Islam, Senior Advocate with MA Samad, Senior Advocate with Subrata Chowdhury, Advocate instructed by Sujia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner. 
TH Khan, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------- Respondents Nos. 1-3.

Government of Bangladesh and others ------- Respondents
case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated the 6th day of September, 2007  passed by the High Court Division in  Appeal from Original Decree (FA)  No. 80 of 1998).
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J : This petition for Leave to Appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 6-9-2007 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 80 of 1998 allowing the appeal setting aside those dated 27-11-1997 of the Sub- ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong in Other Suit No. 120 of 1993 thereby dismissing the same.

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that the plaintiff company is a private limited company incorporated under the Companies Act, 1913 and is a recognised company and it had got commendable certificate from the Government as a foreign exchange earner and also got President's Medal and it is stated that the suit land originally belonged to a company which was a British Company incorporated in London as "Ralli Brothers" and after the liberation of the country the said property had been declared as an abandoned property under President's Order No. 16 of 1972 and it was notified in the Gazette and on 3rd April, 1975 an administrator was appointed by the Government to look after the property and as the same action had not been in accordance with law the Government of Bangladesh had entered into an agreement with the "Ralli Brothers" for purchase of the said company along with its properties on 23-2-1977 and thereafter, the defendant No.1, namely the Government, became the owner of the property and thereafter the said suit land had been transferred to and vested in Bangladesh Jute Corporation by operation of law and it was done under section 19 of Bangladesh Jute Corporation Ordinance and in the said property there were some properties which had been lying as unused property and the Government decided to transfer those properties and on this score the Government constituted a sale committee and the said sale committee took steps in this regard. The defendant No. 3 published a tender for sale of the suit land in the daily newspaper on 20-6-1992 vide Tender No.2 of 1992 and in the said tender the "Kha" schedule property had been included in item No.6 and after publication of the said tender notice the plaintiff had submitted a tender on 20-7-1992 amounting to Taka 6,02,51,000 and as per the terms and conditions of the tender the plaintiff had deposited Taka 60,25,100 as earnest money in the Government Treasury.
